French Foreign Legion recruitment fitness

ENTRY FITNESS TEST

At a glance

The Legion publishes two recruitment fitness evaluations and a swimming recommendation. The published minimum is not a prediction of acceptance into the Legion.

FEATURED ACTIVITYLuc Léger (beep test)Level 5 minimum

What the test includes

  • Luc Léger (beep test) — Level 5 minimum
  • Strict pull-ups — Numeric minimum not stated
  • Swimming — 25 m unaided strongly recommended

Some programmes include more than the activities listed here.

Test protocol and standards

The Legion publishes two recruitment fitness evaluations and a swimming recommendation. The published minimum is not a prediction of acceptance into the Legion.

Official information checked 2026-11-24. Confirm current requirements with the test publisher.

ActivityPublished requirementHow it works
Luc Léger (beep test)Level 5 minimumProgressive 20 m shuttles to an audio signal; see course illustration below.
Strict pull-upsNumeric minimum not statedOverhand grip; begin with arms straight, raise chin above the bar, return to full extension.
Swimming25 m unaided strongly recommendedThis is a recommendation, not a published pass threshold.

Scoring and scope

Use the actual recruitment recording and assessor instructions. The public recruitment page does not state a pull-up number or a missed-beep rule. The swimming recommendation is not a mandatory score.

  • French recruitment page
  • General French 20 m protocol (not Legion scoring rules)

How the Luc Léger (beep test) works

How to run the beep test

  1. Measure two parallel lines 20 metres apart on a flat, non-slip surface. Use the correct recording and leave space to turn.
  2. Start at line A; run to line B in time with the next signal. If early, wait for the signal rather than sprinting ahead.
  3. Turn at the line and run back. The recording progressively increases the pace. Continue until the assessor ends the test.
  4. Record the last accepted level and shuttle. The Legion publishes level 5 as its minimum; it does not publish its exact missed-beep rule on the recruitment page.

Do not use the UK Police 15 metre recording, a shorter lane or a weighted pack. The general French protocol is linked above for context; its exact rules should not be assumed to be Legion rules.

How to prepare

Independent training guidance, not official test instructions. Scale sessions to your current capacity and recover between demanding efforts.

  • Measure a flat 20 m lane and learn the turns at a comfortable pace.
  • Build easy running and separate short shuttle sessions.
  • Practise strict pull-ups using assistance when needed; leave recovery between hard sessions.

Putting it into a training week

Choose two or three repeatable sessions addressing the listed movements and aerobic demand. Leave recovery between harder efforts; record comparable results rather than testing maximally every week.

Common mistakes

  • Using the UK 15 m course or incompatible audio.
  • Counting partial pull-ups or treating the published minimum as a guarantee of selection.

What to log

Record the audio version, last accepted level and shuttle, valid pull-ups and swim distance separately.

Avoid repeated maximal tests and sudden load increases. Stop if pain, dizziness or unusual symptoms occur; use qualified supervision where appropriate.

Official test instructions

The organisation running the test is the best place to check the latest rules and requirements.
